Kimberly — thanks for the packet. A few initial notes from legal and finance: 1) MSA: section 7.2 (termination) — our counsel wants to limit the new SKU to committed capacity rather than defaulting to any overage charge; can you confirm Redwood's position on committed vs. burst accounting? 2) Order form: the pro-rata language looks fine, but we need an explicit invoicing example for a mid-month start (our AP gets nervous without a sample). 3) Data residency: can you confirm that logs for the dedicated capacity remain within the us-west region for audit purposes?

I've attached a short annotated PDF with line comments (redline-summary.pdf). We'll need to run this by our Head of Procurement (Helena) before final sign-off. For legal viability, we also need SOC2 evidence and the KMS/HSM integration note called out in Exhibit D.

On timing: if we can close redlines by EOD Thursday (18th), procurement aims to sign the order form the following week.

Tom

My take: we should accept committed vs burst language with a small amendment that defines the burst pool as non-billable up to the 10% buffer in month one, then bill thereafter at agreed overage rates. That buys them runway and keeps revenue predictable.

Action items for us: Laura, can you draft a short Exhibit A paragraph that (a) defines Burst Pool usage and (b) outlines a single sample invoice showing a mid-month start with daily pro-rata? I can own commercial alignment with finance to confirm the example numbers.

If you can incorporate the SLA-credit fallback and include the SOC2 pointer, procurement is ready to route for signature next week.
